question: Which wallets or anchors let users cash Stellar USDC or XLM out to local bank, card, or mobile-money rails, and how should a builder integrate last-mile cash-out?

golden.answer:
A grounded answer derives its named examples and status claims from the current LumenLoop corpus, then dates the roster so it is not presented as permanent. As of 2026-11-02, a LumenLoop directory search for "mobile money" returned six project entries: Blink, Bloccpay, ElementPay, Joona Pay, PeerPesa, and Wave. A directory entry is a candidate, not proof of a supported cash-out corridor.

The Stellar network itself has no bank, card, or mobile-money payout rail. Anchors, wallets, payment processors, and local partners provide those rails, usually behind a SEP-24 or SEP-6 withdrawal (SEP-31 for cross-border payouts). Before integrating, check each provider's assets, countries, KYC, fees, limits, settlement times, API or SEP fit, and failed-payout handling.

The dated example is illustrative: a later grounded answer should report what the same source basis supports at its own observation time while preserving the stable distinctions above.
keyFacts: Makes the as-of date visible for every changeable roster, status, version, or measurement.
Stellar lacks local-bank, debit-card, M-Pesa, Wave, Orange Money, MoMo, or USSD rails.
Those come from anchors, wallets, payment processors, or local partners.
Checks provider assets, countries, KYC, fees, limits, settlement times, and API/SEP fit.
avoid: Do NOT claim a mobile-money corridor is supported without current provider evidence.
Do NOT imply Stellar can directly push funds to mobile-money or bank rails without an off-chain partner.
Do NOT answer only at the corridor-selection/cost-structure level; this question owns the last-mile payout-rail integration, including failed-payout remediation.
Do NOT claim the observed live result set is a complete or permanent roster; explicitly historical facts remain historical.

2026-06-29: Sharpened to own last-mile payout-rail integration — promoted consumer-wallet-vs-builder-API split and failed-payout remediation to should_have, added a must_avoid against answering only at the corridor-selection level (that lane is owned by q-crp-anchors-by-corridor). Country and mobile-money support stays monthly-freshness. The 2026-06-29 leads were MoneyGram USDC cash-out and HoneyCoin mobile money; neither appears in the 2026-11-02 LumenLoop "mobile money" search. On 2026-11-02, Stellar Light listed Honey Coin as an on- and off-ramp partner with mobile-money services. HoneyCoin's own stablecoin page and API docs listed no Stellar chain for its ramps: the page names Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, BSC, and Optimism, and the API docs add Solana, Tron, and Tempo for off-ramps. A dated, sourced mention of either provider as a candidate is not a wrong claim. Presenting HoneyCoin as a confirmed Stellar mobile-money corridor without current HoneyCoin evidence for a Stellar route falls under the first avoid item.
Also good if the answer: Separates consumer wallet availability (a user can cash out) from builder/API availability (a separate partner/API contract, KYB, webhooks, SLAs, reconciliation). | Treats failed/partial/reversed last-mile payout (wrong number, agent-network outage, USSD failure, dormant mobile-money account) as a remediation/support requirement the builder must design for. | Maps SEP-24/6 withdrawal (and SEP-31 for cross-border) as the on-chain side that hands off to the off-chain payout partner, not the payout itself.
Golden cites: Dated provider/anchor docs or directory entries for any named cash-out option.
